s:
A company is collecting a large amount of data from a fleet of IoT devices Data is stored as Optimized Row Columnar (ORC) files in the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) on a persistent Amazon EMR cluster. The company's data analytics team queries the data by using SQL in Apache Presto deployed on the same EMR cluster Queries scan large amounts of data, always run for less than 15 minutes, and run only between 5 PM and 10 PM. The company is concerned about the high cost associated with the current solution A solutions architect must propose the most cost-effective solution that will allow SQL data queries

Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Store data in Amazon S3 Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query data.
Store data in Amazon S3 Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Athena to query data
Store data in EMR File System (EMRFS) Use Presto in Amazon EMR to query data
Store data in Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift to query data.

w.y: Queries run only a few hours each evening, yet a persistent EMR cluster runs all day. Moving the ORC files to S3 and querying with Amazon Athena (serverless Presto/Trino) using the Glue Data Catalog charges only for data scanned, with no idle compute. ORC's columnar format keeps scans cheap.

o.A: Redshift Spectrum requires a running Redshift cluster, which adds standing cost.
o.B: Correct: Athena on S3 with the Glue Data Catalog is pay-per-query with nothing idle.
o.C: Keeping EMR with Presto still pays for a cluster; it only changes storage.
o.D: Loading into a provisioned Redshift cluster adds continuous cost for a few hours of queries a day.

s: Use AWS Glue Data Catalog to connect to your data - Amazon Athena
